The Improving Law Enforcement Officer Safety and Wellness Through Data Act (S.1418) demands 3 separate DOJ reports analyzing attacks on officers, training programs, and mental health resources. But here’s the problem: the FBI’s Law Enforcement Officers Killed and Assaulted (LEOKA) database already tracks line-of-duty deaths. S.1418’s Section 3(a)(10) redundantly orders DOJ to study merging LEOKA with "09C Justifiable Homicide" data—a bureaucratic circle-jerk.

Meanwhile, the COPS Hiring Program shoveled $224.5M in 2023 to agencies struggling with recruitment, yet this bill allocates zero dollars for bulletproof vests or PTSD counseling. The Thin Blue Line Act’s call for harsher penalties aligns with accountability, but real support means slashing red tape, not commissioning more studies while cops bleed.

Fund gear, not gridlock.
